subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window & latency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finco.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finco.com>
Cc:

Subject: Follow-up & SLO clarifications from today’s call — context window / latency impact

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great speaking with you this morning — thanks for walking through the FinCo GenAssist workflow. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the right serving profile:

Recap of requirements (from the call):
- Primary model: multi-turn assistant with retrieval-augmented context (RAG).
- Typical input: user question + retrieved docs, median input size ~6k tokens, 95th percentile ~18k tokens.
- Expected output: concise summary + action items, avg 150–400 tokens, occasionally up to 2k tokens for long explanations.
- Traffic profile: pilot ~50 QPS, peak expected to 200 QPS during market open.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~120, but backend may fan-out to generate multiple candidates concurrently.
- Latency SLO: target p95 generation latency < 800 ms for standard queries; for large-context queries acceptable SLO up to 1.5s if streaming is enabled.
- Streaming: important for UX on long outputs — client expects partial tokens as they are generated.

Open questions for sizing / next steps (please confirm):
1) Is the 18k token context hard cap per request (input + output), or can you limit retrieved context on the server side?
2) For the 2k-token occasional outputs, are those rare (<1% of requests) or tied to specific product flows we should treat as a separate class?
3) Do you have sample payloads (input JSONs) we can use for an internal perf run? If so, could you drop them in the Drive link above?

I’m attaching a short SLO worksheet (slo_requirements.xlsx) and our initial Redwood perf profile PDF with notes on how context window affects throughput/latency.

Next steps:
- If you can confirm answers to Q1–Q3, I’ll loop in infra (Aditya) to propose Dedicated/reserved capacity options and a perf-run plan.
- We’ll also propose streaming + chunking approach and a fallback model variant for very large contexts.

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up & SLO clarifications from today’s call — context window / latency impact

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Q1: 18k tokens is what our retrieval returns today for long context users; it is not a strict cap, but upstream apps expect all retrieved content to be passed through. We could consider trimming to the top N docs but would prefer to keep the first-pass identical.
- Q2: 2k-token outputs are ~2% of requests (mostly for root-cause analysis and regulatory transcripts).
- Q3: I uploaded three sample payloads to the Drive link: short.json (~800 tokens input), mid.json (~6k tokens), and long.json (~18k tokens).

On latency / streaming: we strongly prefer streaming for the mid and long cases so the UI shows progressive answers. Target p95 of <800 ms is what the product owner asked for across the board; if that’s not feasible for long requests we can relax to 1.5s but need to understand perceived UX impact.

Let us know what info you need from infra/perf to size Dedicated capacity vs hosted. Also, curious if Redwood can provide partial responses (streaming) while continuing to process remaining context, or if streaming requires finishing full attention pass first.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product, GenAssist | FinCo Capital
alex.turner@finco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finco.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & SLO clarifications from today’s call — context window / latency impact

Alex — perfect, thanks for confirming and for the sample payloads. High-level notes from an inference / perf perspective (copied Aditya for sizing):

1) Context window and latency:
- End-to-end generation latency scales roughly with: model compute per token * (input_length + output_length) / effective throughput + overheads (KV cache ops, attention kernel costs for long context).
- For autoregressive models, long input contexts (e.g., 18k tokens) significantly increase the first-token latency because attention must process the full input. For generation of long outputs, streaming helps perceived latency but does not reduce total compute — it just amortizes perceived wait.

2) Streaming behavior:
- Redwood streaming can emit partial tokens as soon as the decoder emits them. For very long inputs, there are two common approaches:
  a) Incremental/early decode: chunk the input, produce a partial decode on the most relevant chunk(s) while background processing completes the full context — good UX but requires careful retrieval ranking.
  b) Full-context decode with progressive emit: compute attention across full context first (higher initial latency) and then stream output tokens.
- Which approach we recommend depends on how critical the p95 first-byte latency is for long queries. If you need <800 ms p95 even on 18k inputs, chunking + progressive refinement is typically the only viable option without massive reserved capacity.

3) Throughput and concurrency tradeoffs:
- Batchability helps throughput but hurts tail latency. If you have strict p95 SLOs, we recommend configuring small max-batch sizes (1–4) and enabling smart routing to dedicate lower-latency nodes for interactive traffic.
- For pilot QPS (50) vs peak (200), Dedicated reserved pools with autoscaling burst capacity usually provide the best predictable p95. We can sketch compute-hours and GPU/instance counts once Aditya has the sample payload perf numbers.

4) Practical recommendations:
- Treat the 2% of 2k-token outputs as a separate class: route to a different model variant or different queue with relaxed SLO (e.g., p95 1.5–2s) to protect interactive traffic.
- Enable streaming for mid/long flows and implement client-side optimistic rendering for partial answers.
- Consider a retrieval limit (e.g., top 5 docs) with on-demand expansion if users request more context.

Next steps (action items):
- Aditya: can you run a perf sweep on the three sample payloads (short / mid / long) using the Redwood perf profile and paste results to the Drive link? Focus on p50/p95 for first byte and end-to-end generation for 150-token and 2k-token outputs.
- Alex / Priya: confirm whether you can accept a separate queue for the 2% long outputs or whether all requests must be served from a single latency class.
- I’ll follow up with a Dedicated sizing note and a draft mutual action plan.

If helpful, I attached our Redwood perf profile (redwood_perf_profile.pdf) with notes on kernel choices, quantization, and expected token/sec on common GPU types.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: redwood_perf_profile.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finco.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finco.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinCo perf sizing — please review samples + propose config

Aditya / Jordan — looping you both in following my thread with FinCo (see chain above). They uploaded three payloads to Drive and are asking for a perf sweep focused on p50/p95 first-byte and end-to-end for 150-token and 2k-token outputs. Key constraints:
- 18k-token long contexts are common for some users; p95 target is <800 ms but FinCo said they can relax to 1.5s for those cases if streaming is enabled.
- Pilot traffic ~50 QPS, peak ~200 QPS, concurrent users ~120, with occasional candidate-generation fan-out.
- They prefer streaming UX.

Please do an initial run on our standard 8xA100 profile and a 4xH100 profile if available. Capture: first-byte p50/p95, end-to-end p50/p95 for both 150-token and 2k-token outputs, and note memory footprint (KV cache) for the long context. Also include a note on whether chunked/incremental decode would materially improve p95 on the 18k sample.

Target: can you have a short write-up and numbers by EOD tomorrow? If you need more time, let me know. I’ll sync back with FinCo once we have the numbers to propose Dedicated sizing and queueing strategy.

Thanks — Marissa
